units.translation: In the Great Ehoiai (Hes. fr. 148 Rz.²) it is said that Endymion was carried up to heaven by Zeus, and that he fell in love with Hera; he was deceived by a phantom of a cloud, and after being cast out he came down.

To Hades. Epimenides (3 B 14 Diels-Kranz) says that he, while spending time among the gods, fell in love with Hera, and that therefore, when Zeus became angry, he asked to sleep forever. Some say that because of his great righteousness he was deified and asked from Zeus to sleep always.

Some reject the myth about Endymion's sleep. For they say that he was fond of hunting, and at night he hunted by the light of the moon because the wild beasts come out at that time to their pastures, and during the days he rested in a cave, so that some thought he was always sleeping. Others allegorize the myth, saying that Endymion was the first to attempt philosophy concerning the heavens, and that the moon provided him with starting points in its illuminations and movements, for which reason he spent his nights on these studies and did not sleep, but slept during the day. Some say that Endymion was in fact a lover of sleep, from which comes the proverb 'Endymion's sleep' applied to those who sleep a lot or do something carelessly so as to seem to be asleep.
